comment: Teleop wire messages (DESIGN §10). Every message: 12-byte header (magic 'RTGS', version u16, type u16, payload length u32), then the fields in order, little-endian. Arrays and strings are prefixed by a u32 element count (strings: UTF-8 bytes). Poses are in the server's canonical frame: metres, Z-up, +X forward; quaternions w, x, y, z. Regenerate the codecs with tools/gen_stream_codec.py.

messages.name: StreamStart
messages.doc: Client -> server: opens (or restarts) a stream with its human skeleton.
fields: parent joint index, -1 for the root
J x 3, joint offset from its parent in the rest pose (m)

messages.name: HumanFrame
messages.doc: Client -> server: one frame of a stream.
fields: capture time of the frame (s, client clock)
J x 3, local joint translations in the parent frame (m; the rest offsets unless the joint moves, e.g. root and hips)
J x 4, local joint rotations relative to the parent

messages.name: StreamInfo
messages.doc: Server -> client: reply to StreamStart (status 0) or an error about a stream (status 1).
fields: names of RobotFrame.contact entries (human contact groups)
output lag behind the newest input (s)

messages.name: RobotFrame
messages.doc: Server -> client: the robot pose solved for one HumanFrame.
fields: N (rad/s), backward difference of the emitted poses
weighted tracking cost of the solve
bits: 1 velocity clamped, 2 cold start, 4 unsupported, 8 penetration, 16 environment support, 32 flight, 64 frames dropped
